<header class="ws-head"><span class="ws-kicker">Day 2 · 11:30–16:15 · Technical module 7 · serves M7</span><h2>Team build, showcase and the journey together<span class="ws-badge">Draft</span></h2><p class="ws-carries">Can each team change one app in the journey and then run the whole journey live, from a birth abroad to a clinic back home to the family travelling again?</p></header>
<h3>Sessions</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Team build</span><span class="ws-sheet">11:30–12:30 · 60 min</span></span><b>Team build, part 1</b><p>Each team takes one app in the journey. Everything is pre-configured, so there is no Android Studio. You run the app, read how its configuration works, and change it. Test with the vaccination cards.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Roy Munge, Elly Nandi, Fikri, Simon Njoroge · <span class="ws-t">Supports</span>One per team</p></div><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Team build</span><span class="ws-sheet">13:30–14:25 · 55 min</span></span><b>Team build, part 2</b><p>Finish the change, test it with the cards, and get ready to show it.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Roy Munge, Elly Nandi, Fikri, Simon Njoroge · <span class="ws-t">Supports</span>One per team</p></div><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Showcase</span><span class="ws-sheet">14:25–15:00 · 35 min</span></span><b>Team presentations</b><p>Each team shows what it built, about seven minutes each. Volunteers present.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Fred Hersch (chair)</p><p class="ws-confirm">Proposed</p></div><div class="ws-card"><span class="ws-mod-h"><span class="ws-step">Team build</span><span class="ws-sheet">15:30–16:15 · 45 min</span></span><b>Putting the journey together</b><p>Volunteers run the whole journey on the demo system, each using their own piece. This is the rehearsal for the finale.</p><p class="ws-who"><span class="ws-t">Leads</span>Roy Munge, Simon Njoroge · <span class="ws-t">Supports</span>A volunteer from each team</p><p class="ws-confirm">Proposed</p></div></div>
<h3>By the end you can</h3><ul><li>Run your app and find where its configuration lives</li><li>Make one change and see it work</li><li>Have a working piece you can show in under seven minutes</li></ul>
<h3>Where it meets the journey</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><b>Registered at home, and referred</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>CHW app team: the registration form, the household, the referral.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>Which one configuration change would make the CHW app fit your country's household register?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J3a/">J3a</a><b>The clinic confirms the cards are genuine</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Clinic app team: the verifier and its trust store.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>How would your clinic app load your country's trust list, and how often would it refresh it?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0a/">J4.0a</a><b>One phone holds the whole family’s records</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Family app team: one phone, one profile and one link per member.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>How should the family app separate each member's records on a shared phone?</p></div><div class="ws-card"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.1/">J4.1</a><b>A Taifafeki doctor sees the full history</b><p><span class="ws-t">What the system does</span>Viewer app team: open the link, enter the passcode, read the records.</p><p><span class="ws-q">Technical question</span>What must the viewer show the clinician about where the records came from?</p></div></div>
<h3>Technical questions for the room</h3><ul class="ws-qs"><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a><span>Which one configuration change would make the CHW app fit your country's household register?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J3a/">J3a</a><span>How would your clinic app load your country's trust list, and how often would it refresh it?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0a/">J4.0a</a><span>How should the family app separate each member's records on a shared phone?</span></li><li><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.1/">J4.1</a><span>What must the viewer show the clinician about where the records came from?</span></li></ul>
<h3>The four teams</h3><div class="ws-cards"><div class="ws-card"><b>CHW app</b><span class="ws-muted">The health worker's phone</span><p>Scan a vaccination card, add the child to the household, and refer them to a clinic.</p><span class="ws-steps-inline"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2a/">J2a</a> <a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J2b/">J2b</a></span></div><div class="ws-card"><b>Clinic app</b><span class="ws-muted">The nurse's tablet</span><p>Receive the referral, verify the card against the trust list, and plan the next visit.</p><span class="ws-steps-inline"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J3a/">J3a</a> <a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J3b/">J3b</a></span></div><div class="ws-card"><b>Family app</b><span class="ws-muted">The parent's phone</span><p>Hold the family's records and share a child's record as a health link.</p><span class="ws-steps-inline"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0a/">J4.0a</a> <a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.0b/">J4.0b</a></span></div><div class="ws-card"><b>Viewer app</b><span class="ws-muted">The clinic abroad</span><p>Open a shared health link and read the records behind it.</p><span class="ws-steps-inline"><a class="ws-step" href="en/smart-trust-demo/journeys/smart-trust-demo/workshops/dpi-h-policy-track/walkthrough/J4.1/">J4.1</a></span></div></div>
<h3>Terms at those steps</h3><div class="ws-terms"><a href="glossary.html#term-client-registry" title="The Client Registry is the national authoritative source of health-specific person identity. It is the foundational health-sector component that maintains a unique, verifiable identity record for every person who accesses or is eligible to access health services within a jurisdiction.">Client Registry</a><a href="glossary.html#term-civil-registration-and-vital-statistics" title="Birth registration can start a child's immunization record.">Civil registration and vital statistics</a><a href="glossary.html#term-point-of-service-application" title="Point-of-service applications are end-user application components (IT systems or software tools) used by individuals directly engaged in healthcare—such as clinicians, community health workers, and patients—that enable interaction with the broader healthcare ecosystem.">Point-of-Service Applications</a><a href="glossary.html#term-facility-workforce-and-product-registries" title="Authoritative lists of health facilities, health workers, and products such as vaccines and their batches.">Facility, workforce and product registries</a><a href="glossary.html#term-consent" title="A person's permission for their data to be used or shared. Rules for minors and dependants differ by country.">Consent</a><a href="glossary.html#term-interoperability" title="Interoperability is the standards-based capability of heterogeneous information systems to communicate, exchange data, and use the exchanged information to execute functions effectively.">Interoperability</a><a href="glossary.html#term-trust-list" title="A published list of keys accepted as valid issuers. The GDHCN shares these between countries.">Trust list</a><a href="glossary.html#term-global-digital-health-certification-network" title="WHO Global Digital Health Certification Network. A trust network so countries can verify each other's health documents. Countries onboard per use case.">Global Digital Health Certification Network</a><a href="glossary.html#term-trust-anchor" title="The national authority whose key vouches for the health sector's signers.">Trust anchor</a><a href="glossary.html#term-public-key-infrastructure" title="The keys, certificates and rules that make digital signatures trustworthy.">Public key infrastructure</a><a href="glossary.html#term-digital-signature" title="A cryptographic seal made with the issuer's private key. Verifiers check it with the matching public key.">Digital signature</a><a href="glossary.html#term-issuer-holder-verifier" title="The three roles: who signs the credential, who keeps it, and who checks it.">Issuer · holder · verifier</a><a href="glossary.html#term-verifiable-credential" title="A digitally signed statement, such as a vaccination record, that anyone can check is genuine and unaltered.">Verifiable credential</a><a href="glossary.html#term-digital-wallet" title="An app where a person holds their credentials. A signed paper QR code can play the same role.">Digital wallet</a><a href="glossary.html#term-personal-health-record" title="Health information the person can see and control, for example in a wallet or citizen app.">Personal health record</a><a href="glossary.html#term-lifelong-health-record" title="The Lifelong Health Record (LHR) is one or more governed data repositories, whether physically consolidated or virtually federated, that collectively maintain a longitudinal, person-centred record of an individual's key health information across care settings and over their lifetime.">Lifelong Health Record</a><a href="glossary.html#term-international-patient-summary" title="A standard minimal health summary, including immunizations, readable across borders.">International Patient Summary</a><a href="glossary.html#term-health-information-exchange" title="The layer that routes data securely between systems.">Health information exchange</a></div>
